sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Palm Beach Gardens, FL?
sections.html:
Yes. Palm Beach Gardens sellers can close quickly with a cash buyer or take the slower route of a full listing, and the right choice depends on your home's condition and your deadline. This is a high-value market, so the tax and recording details deserve more attention here than in most Florida cities.

The sections below cover the city's planned origins, Census figures, and the Palm Beach County tax rules that apply when you sell.

sections.h2: How was Palm Beach Gardens built?
sections.html:
Palm Beach Gardens began as a planned community. On March 20, 1959, John D. MacArthur announced plans to develop about 4,000 acres for 55,000 people, according to the city's About page.

His preferred name, Palm Beach city, was refused, so he chose Palm Beach Gardens to match his garden city plan. He directed that streets and construction go around mature trees such as the banyans, and he built churches first. By 1964 he had attracted the Professional Golfers Association, whose clubhouse was completed in March 1965. In 1999 the MacArthur Foundation sold about 14,000 acres, around 5,000 of them in the city, which is why newer neighborhoods carry a 1999 era development pattern.

For a seller, this history explains the mature tree cover, the waterways and the master-planned layout buyers see on many streets.

sections.h2: Does age change how you sell in Palm Beach Gardens?
sections.html:
It can. With about a third of residents age 65 or older, many sellers here are downsizing or moving after decades in the same house, and several Florida benefits are tied to age and service.

  • A county or city ordinance may allow an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners 65 and older within the household income limit. Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser whether your address qualifies.
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount equal to their VA disability percentage.
  • A homestead tax deferral application goes to the tax collector by March 31, and a permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent of household income.
  • Homestead ends once the home is rented or is no longer your permanent residence.

If you are selling to move to a different Florida home, portability may let you carry up to $500,000 of the difference between just value and assessed value, as stated in the statute. Chapter 2026-239 amendments to that section first apply to the 2027 tax roll.

sections.h2: How do taxes and fees work when a house sells here?
sections.html:
The property appraiser values the house each January 1 and the tax collector bills in November. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

The documentary stamp tax on a deed in Palm Beach County is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Miami-Dade is the one county with a different rate, so this is the standard Florida figure. Recording charges apply on top, and the statute sets the first page at $5.00 and each added page at $4.00, with extra trust fund and technology charges per page. Your title agent can price all of this before you accept an offer.

  • Value challenges: file a petition within 25 days of the August TRIM notice.
  • Exemption denials: petition the value adjustment board within 30 days of the denial letter being mailed.

sections.h2: What if the Palm Beach Gardens house has a lender problem or a tax lien?
sections.html:
A judicial foreclosure sale happens at least 20 days after final judgment, and no more than 35 days unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period. The high bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent, and the sale stands confirmed if no objection arrives within 10 days of the certificate of sale. A homestead owner is told to check with the clerk within 10 days after sale for any surplus.

Tax certificates follow a separate track. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, and certificates sell by June 1 to whoever bids the lowest interest rate. A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, with notice going to the owner and any mortgage holder. If you are anywhere on either track, talk to a title agent about payoff figures before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What kind of sale suits a Palm Beach Gardens home?
sections.html:
Choose based on condition, equity and time. A higher priced home usually earns more on the open market if it is staged and updated, and a direct cash sale fits an owner who wants certainty.

  • Open market: a stronger price if you can wait through showings and buyer financing.
  • Cash as-is: fewer contingencies and a date you choose.
  • Estate sales: a personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable for stamps, and Florida's own estate tax no longer applies.

sections.h2: What can a Palm Beach Gardens owner do about an unwanted occupant?
sections.html:
Florida lets an owner or agent submit a verified complaint to the sheriff to remove people occupying a residence without any right to be there. The statute lists conditions: there is no tenancy, the person is not a relative, the property is not open to the public, the owner has directed them to leave, and no court case is pending.

False statements expose an owner to damages, including statutory damages equal to triple the fair market rent plus costs and attorney fees. If someone is a tenant, use the notice process instead: three days for nonpayment, with weekends and holidays excluded, or seven days to cure certain lease violations. Vacant homes in a retiree-heavy market can attract this problem, so check on seasonal or inherited properties regularly.

faqs.q: Is Palm Beach Gardens in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes. Property taxes are valued by the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser and collected by the county tax collector. The city's own site links to the property appraiser's page to verify residency.

faqs.q: How old is Palm Beach Gardens?
faqs.a: The city's founding announcement was made on March 20, 1959, when John D. MacArthur announced plans for about 4,000 acres. It is a planned community rather than a historic town.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the standard Florida rate. Only Miami-Dade differs.

faqs.q: Can I defer property tax as a senior?
faqs.a: Possibly. File Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31. A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the portion above 3 percent of household income. Ask the tax collector for eligibility.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings after selling?
faqs.a: Part of it, if you buy a new Florida homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one. File DR-501T with DR-501 by March 1.
